paper.title: An Optimal Algorithm for Bandit and Zero-Order Convex Optimization with Two-Point Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit convex optimization with two-point feedback (general norm / mirror descent)
unmapped: learner plays w_t in W (suffers f_t(w_t)) and separately queries two points w_t +/- delta_t u_t, which may lie slightly outside W
learner needs a regularizer r with sup_W r <= R^2 (R known) that is 1-strongly convex w.r.t. a norm whose dual satisfies a 4th-moment condition
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t$, the adversary picks a convex function $f_t$ on $\reals^d$, which is not revealed to the learner. The learner then chooses a point $\bw_t$ from some known and closed convex set $\Wcal\subseteq \reals^d$, and suffers a loss $f_t(\bw_t)$. As feedback, the learner may choose two points $\bw'_t,\bw''_t\in \Wcal$ and receive $f_t(\bw_t'),f_t(\bw_t'')$.

settings.name_in_paper: Two-point bandit convex optimization on the simplex, L1-Lipschitz losses
unmapped: loss functions f_t are convex and G_1-Lipschitz w.r.t. the L1 norm
query points may lie slightly outside W
settings.definition_quote: the $1$-norm, $\norm{\cdot}_1$, the domain $\Wcal$ is the simplex in $\reals^d$, $d>1$ ... Suppose $f_t$ for all $t$ is $G_1$-Lipschitz with respect to the $L_1$ norm.

algorithms.name: Two-Point Bandit Convex Optimization Algorithm (mirror descent with symmetric two-point gradient estimator)

symbols.p_star: bound on (E||u||_*^4)^{1/4} for u uniform on the unit sphere
symbols.G_2: Lipschitz constant of f_t w.r.t. the 2-norm
symbols.R: sup_W r(w) <= R^2 for the 1-strongly convex regularizer r

conditions: r 1-strongly convex w.r.t. norm ||.|| with sup_W r <= R^2

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: If $\eta = \frac{R}{p_{*} G_2 \sqrt{dT}}$, and $\delta_t$ chosen such that $\delta_t\leq p_*R\sqrt{\frac{d}{T}}$, then the sequence $\bw_1,\ldots,\bw_T$ generated by the algorithm satisfies the following for any $T$ and $\bw^*\in\Wcal$: \E[\frac{1}{T}\sum f_t(\bw_t)-\frac{1}{T}\sum f_t(\bw^*)] \leq c~p_{*} G_2R\sqrt{\frac{d}{T}}, where $c$ is some numerical constant.

results.notes: Paper bounds average regret; multiplied by T. Expectation over learner randomness for any fixed w*. Registry match to osgd_two_point is approximate (mirror descent generalization).

tuning: eta, delta_t as in Theorem 1 with p_star = 1

source.label: cor:1
source.quote: Suppose $f_t$ for all $t$ is $G_1$-Lipschitz with respect to the $L_1$ norm. Then using $\norm{\cdot}=\norm{\cdot}_1$ and $r(\bw)=\sum_{i=1}^{d}w_i\log(d w_i)$, it holds for some constant $c$ and any $\bw^*\in\Wcal$ that ... \leq c~G_1 \sqrt{\frac{d\log^2(d)}{T}}.

results.notes: Average regret multiplied by T. Optimal up to a log factor per paper.
